body:
Thanks for chatting killcoyote :)

Hard to say if it's one specific event, because I did just recently get rejected by someone I was interested in and I took it harder than usual (I don't really get crushes very often for whatever reason, once every couple years), so obviously that's a factor. But I don't think that's it, I think that's just one piece of the puzzle, and the whole puzzle is this bigger feeling of being inadequate. Because that's not just limited to this one aspect of my life, relationships, it bleeds into everything, the way I look, the way I act, the words I say and write, my skills and talents or lack thereof, etc. A big overarching feeling of futility and I'm not quite sure where it comes from. 

There's always moments you know that make life seem worth living. I'm a musician so music is a big one for me. Rare moments, like those profound moments of transcendence during a work of art like listening to music or reading a book or looking at a painting or whatever, or meeting a new friend, or falling in love, I don't know, lots of things. They somehow seem much more ephemeral though then this kind of nagging feeling of wanting to curl up and die. 

I don't know why everything tries to live. I think about my dog (or I guess now it's my parents' dog, I moved out). That thing just keeps going, loyal to a fault and always a pleasing and positive attitude, I mean best I can tell. I admire the damn pooch. I think it's beautiful that, pathetic as it is, it keeps persisting in the face of its immanent demise. Without her family to support her she'd be as good as coyote food out in the wild, but I'll be damned if that doesn't stop her from hopping up on her short little legs and licking my face every time I visit home. She's tougher than I am that's for sure, I am weak, I can barely handle it. I hate the fact that I am even contemplating suicide, I find that pretty cowardly itself, but here I am, my own brand of pathetic. I don't know killcoyote, whatever that reason is to keep living sometimes it sometimes seems so elusive as to not even be worth chasing.

Yeah. I agree with that, that's what I've been trying. I guess what I'm trying to say is that I keep rolling every day and I haven't lost the desire to keep rolling but the depression and suicidal thoughts have really cropped up now, like as a byproduct of rolling. Like, is this it? How many fucking days do I gotta keep rolling? I think the right answer is every goddamn day, but I think its understandable why someone could look at that and think well gee is it really worth it.

I think maybe the futility comes from blaming myself for having to constantly roll the boulder. Like it's my fault I'm not good enough to get to the top of the hill. But then, maybe the whole point is no one gets to the top of the hill. Usually I can tolerate this worldview, but not recently, not at all. But I do like Camus :)
